title: How the Cole Disaster Drove the U.S. to Develop New Warship Defenses
partialText: The Navy destroyers enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports carry weapons fielded after an American warship was attacked and nearly sunk more than 25 years ago.

title: Strait of Hormuz May Not Return to Normal, Whether It’s Open or Closed
partialText: The energy industry is planning for a future where the choke point on Iran’s southern coast is a lot less important.

title: Europe Wanted a Say on the Iran War, but It’s Still on the Sidelines
partialText: A British-French plan to secure the Strait of Hormuz would give the continent a role. But Tehran and Washington are still calling the shots.

title: Supreme Court Reviews F.C.C.’s Enforcement Power Against Communications Companies
partialText: AT&T and Verizon were penalized millions of dollars for what the agency said was a failure to protect consumer information. The companies say they were deprived of their right to a jury trial.

title: Trump Dismisses a Merger While Seeking Suitors for Spirit Airlines
partialText: As he rejected the idea of a merger of United Airlines and American Airlines, President Trump said someone, including possibly the federal government, should buy or help Spirit.

title: Virginia Redistricting Referendum: What to Watch
partialText: Republicans have built a small advantage from the gerrymandering clash so far, but Virginia voters could change that.

title: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger Stressed Pragmatism, But Politics Hound Her
partialText: Gov. Abigail Spanberger of Virginia has emphasized practical governance as her brand, but the political fight over redistricting has dominated her term so far.

title: A Wish List for John Ternus, the Man Replacing Tim Cook as Apple’s CEO
partialText: John Ternus, an Apple veteran who runs hardware engineering, will take over an extraordinarily profitable company in need of new ideas.

title: Tim Cook Was Very, Very Good at Making Money
partialText: If the Steve Jobs era was defined by technological innovation, the Tim Cook period was one of exceptional financial growth.

title: What to Expect in Apple’s New Era
partialText: Tim Cook’s replacement as chief executive, John Ternus, knows hardware engineering. Can he be a product visionary and a global diplomat?

title: ‘Wagyu’ Used to Guarantee Quality Beef. What Are You Paying for Today?
partialText: Behind the scenes, competing forces battle for the reputation of prestige meat.

title: A Year After U.S.A.I.D.’s Death, Fired Workers Find Few Jobs and Much Loss
partialText: People have plowed through savings, cashed out retirement funds and moved in with relatives. Former U.S.A.I.D. workers estimate that less than half have found full-time work.

title: ‘Donnyland’? Ukraine Proposes Renaming Part of the Donbas in Trump’s Honor
partialText: The proposal reflects a global reality in which governments appeal to President Trump’s vanity in order to get American might on their side.

title: Imprisoned for 30 Years, He Wooed Her With Love Poems
partialText: After a forced confession and a death sentence, a Kurdish poet spent 30 years in jail, where he discovered his voice. His literary champion, to everyone’s surprise, became his life partner.

title: A.I. Is Eliminating Jobs on Wall Street
partialText: “A.I. gives us places to go we haven’t gone,” said one bank’s chief executive.

title: Florida Inquiry Into ChatGPT’s Role in FSU Shooting Shifts to Criminal Investigation
partialText: The investigation focuses on messages between the chatbot and the man accused of killing two people at Florida State University last year.

title: 2 Americans Killed in Mexico Crash Were C.I.A. Members
partialText: The two Americans were killed on Sunday when their vehicle crashed while returning from a counter-cartel operation led by Mexico’s armed forces in the state of Chihuahua.

title: How ‘The Devil Wears Prada 2’ Red Carpet Looks Came Together
partialText: The press tour for “The Devil Wears Prada 2” has been a fashion show for its stars and their stylists, who have relied on group chats, sweatpants and camaraderie to pull it off.

title: Meryl Streep, Anne Hathaway and More Red Carpet Looks from “The Devil Wears Prada 2”
partialText: At a starry premiere at Lincoln Center, fashion industry figures reflected on just how much the original film got right.

title: My Child Died of Measles
partialText: If more people had gotten the vaccine, she might still be here.

title: The Sam Altman Attack Was Wrong. It Also Says Something Important About Silicon Valley.
partialText: The attack against Sam Altman reflects how badly Silicon Valley needs to address the societal consequences of its products.

title: Pain at the Pump
partialText: We look at the changes in gas prices.

title: Japan to Sell More Weapons Abroad, Breaking With Postwar Pacifism
partialText: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi reversed limits on arms exports as Japan faces rising threats from China and unpredictability from its main ally, the United States.

title: Louisiana Killer’s Threats to Himself and Others Hinted at Future Violence
partialText: Shamar Elkins had been suffering severe mental health problems, his family said. His deadly rampage, which killed eight children, has profoundly scarred a community facing rising domestic violence.

title: These Salmon Got High on Cocaine. That Wasn’t the Craziest Part.
partialText: Scientists in Sweden made an unexpected discovery when they exposed the fish to the illegal drug as well as another substance.

title: Harvey Weinstein’s Third Trial on Rape Charge Opens in Manhattan
partialText: Harvey Weinstein is accused of raping an actress in a Manhattan hotel more than a decade ago. After an overturned conviction and a hung jury, he will face the charge once again.
